summary: Poul Tuxen (1880–1955) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Copenhagen (M.A., Ph.D.) under Andersen and Møller, Leipzig under Windisch, and Bonn under Jacobi. In 1928, he became Professor of Indology at Copenhagen, serving until 1951.
Poulami Ray works in history and archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen and was a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held a post at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and served as a professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 2009).
Prabhasa Dharma (1931–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teachers Joshu Sasaki (1967) and Seikaku Hirata.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (1898–1956) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned an M.A. at Calcutta and a State Doctorate at Paris under Sylvain Lévi. He held professorships at Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati.

Prabodh Shirvalkar specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2009, where he became an assistant professor that same year.

Prachi Vatsal is an Indologist and linguist who completed an M.Phil.-Ph.D. at Jawaharlal Nehru University (2016–2023). In 2025, she was appointed Sanskrit Educator at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi.

Pradeep P. Gokhale (born 1953) specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1980, later serving there as an adjunct professor in 2018.
Pragati Sahni works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Damien Keown and serves as an associate professor at the University of Delhi (attested 2026).

Praggnaparamita Biswas works in Indology. She earned her Ph.D. at Banaras Hindu University under Ratna Basu and held posts at Ranaghat College, The Asiatic Society (2017–2021), and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University (2021–2022).

Pragya Jain works in Indology and philosophy, earning an M.Phil. at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University and a Ph.D. at Mohanlal Sukhadia University. Her academic appointments include assistant professor at M. K. Sanghvi College and visiting fellow at Oxford (2025).

Prahlad Pradhan (1910–1982) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Patna University and Visva-Bharati. He served as professor at Utkal University (~1967–1978), principal at Gangadhar Meher University, and held posts at Ravenshaw and Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

Pramod Chandra (1930–2016) was an art historian and Indologist. Educated at Georgetown and the University of Mumbai (Ph.D., 1964), he was a professor at the University of Chicago (1971–1980) and later the Bickford Professor at Harvard University (1980–2004).

Pranabesh Bhattacharya works in Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandira, Visva-Bharati University, and Bankura University (Ph.D., 2025). In 2025, he became an assistant professor at Sri Sathya Sai University for Human Excellence.

Pranav Prakash works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford (attested 2021–2024) and as a Senior Mellon Fellow at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

Pranshu Samdarshi works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He completed an M.Phil. at the University of Delhi (2010–2018) and served as assistant professor at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham (2019–2021) and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (2021).

Prasanna Venkatesh T S works in computational fields and Indology. He has held positions at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College as a Ph.D. research scholar and at the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad.
Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied under Viroj Inthanon and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Mysore (attested 2014).

Prashant Dharmadhikari works in Indology. He held a post at K.G. Joshi College of Arts and N.G. Bedekar College of Commerce and became an assistant professor at the Central University of Gujarat in 2023.

Pratap Chandra Chunder (1919–2008) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Hindu School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, where he was taught by Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.
